en/96b24e63: Before you start. Meena has put ₹1,00,000 into a mutual fund. Then she reads that a fund house has had trouble. Her first fear is simple: is my money gone with it? To answer, you must know who does what in a fund.
en/0331da24: What happens to my money if the AMC goes bust? AMC means asset management company, the firm that manages the fund. Let us watch what changes for you if the AMC fails, and what does not.. What if the AMC goes bust?
en/cd1f1ba2: A made-up fund of ₹50 crore. Meena's ₹10,000 is a small part. The AMC has ₹20 crore of its own money. The securities the fund bought sit with a separate custodian, not with the AMC. Now the AMC fails. Its own money drops to zero. The custodian still holds ₹50 crore of securities, and Meena's units are still hers. The fund can still rise or fall with markets. But an AMC failing is not the same as her money vanishing.. The AMC fails. AMC's own money (₹ crore), 20, 0. Securities with custodian (₹ crore), 50, 50. Meena's units (₹ thousand), 10, 10
en/73036185: A mutual fund is a trust. The sponsor sets it up. Trustees watch over the AMC, which manages the money. A separate custodian holds the securities. The RTA keeps the unit records. SEBI writes the rules and AMFI runs the code of conduct.. Who does what

en/4f9d8083: The riskometer is a gauge on every scheme. It has six levels, from Low to Very High. It is based on what the fund actually holds, and it is updated regularly. en/feb74f8b: SEBI sorts schemes into categories so that funds with the same label follow the same rules. A large cap fund must keep a minimum in large caps, so it cannot drift into small caps. But the label tells you the rules, not the results. Two funds in a category can earn very differently.. What a category label tells you

en/14499cf4: If I do not know the final price, how much do I bid? You can bid at the cut-off, which means you accept whatever final price is set within the band. Your bank blocks the money for the upper price, and releases any extra later.. How to apply
en/63f5c8b2: Meena's application. Price band, ₹180 to ₹190. Shares she wants, 70. Amount blocked, at upper price, ₹13,300. If the final price is ₹185, ₹12,950 is used, the rest is released
en/75cb1276: The issue states a lower and an upper price. Demand from bidders helps set the final price. With ASBA, money is blocked, and is debited only on allotment. Cut-off means you accept the final price set within the band.. True or false
en/99bb6d94: Check yourself. Rohan applies at cut-off in an IPO with a band of ₹180 to ₹190. What does he agree to?
en/4e0d19cd: Check yourself. Meena applies using ASBA with UPI. When is her money actually debited?
en/ac10a63c: Check yourself. What is book building?
en/1e1c0a65: Check yourself. The band is ₹180 to ₹190. Meena wants 70 shares at the upper price. How much is blocked?
en/c5de1e55: Remember. Cut-off: you accept the final price set within the band.. ASBA with UPI blocks money and debits it only on allotment.. Book building uses demand to find the final price.
en/c6a9962e: Allotment and listing. IPOs: how they work and how to judge them · Beginner
en/85e73136: Before you start. An IPO has 10 lakh shares on offer for retail investors. 5 lakh people apply, wanting one lot each. That is far more demand than supply. Not everyone can get shares. A lottery decides.
en/f39b199b: I applied and got nothing. Did I do something wrong? Probably not. When an issue is oversubscribed, retail allotment can be by lottery. Many people receive nothing. It is normal and not a mistake.. When demand is huge
en/3d1480a3: The retail portion offers 10 lakh shares. Applications come in for 40 lakh shares. That is four times the offer, so the issue is 4 times subscribed. Not everyone can be allotted shares, so a lottery may decide.. A made-up oversubscribed issue. Retail portion (lakh shares), 10, 40
en/49464e1e: Four terms. Oversubscription, More bids than shares on offer. Allotment, Giving shares to applicants, by lottery if retail demand is large. Listing gain, Listing price less issue price. It can also be a loss. Investor categories, Retail, non-institutional and qualified institutional buyers
en/ad3cd194: Check yourself. An issue has 10 lakh shares on offer and receives bids for 30 lakh. What is this?
en/9c843e29: Check yourself. Meena applied in an oversubscribed IPO and got no shares. What is the likely reason?
en/bcfe9d32: Check yourself. Rohan's IPO shares list at ₹210 against an issue price of ₹190. What is the gain per share?
en/4f001a90: Check yourself. Why is a listing gain not guaranteed?
en/d1f9aefc: Remember. Oversubscription means more bids than shares. Retail allotment may be a lottery.. A listing gain is listing price less issue price. It can be a loss.. Missing out in a lottery is normal.
en/93dd2cec: Judging an IPO. IPOs: how they work and how to judge them · Beginner
en/fd350967: Before you start. Two IPOs raise ₹1,000 crore each. In the first, the company gets all of it to build new plants. In the second, the existing owners sell their shares and the company gets nothing. Same size, very different meaning.
en/79b193b1: Both IPOs raise the same amount. Why does it matter? A fresh issue puts money into the company. An offer for sale puts money into the pockets of existing shareholders. Check which, and check what the company plans to do with its money.. Where does the money go?
en/7e4d563b: Reading an IPO. Fresh issue, New shares, and the money goes to the company. Offer for sale, Existing holders sell, and the money goes to them. Use of proceeds, How the company says it will spend the money. Valuation, The price compared with earnings, assets or similar companies
en/62abd425: New shares bring new money into the business. In an offer for sale, existing holders receive the money. Use of proceeds says whether the money repays debt or builds a plant. Even a good brand can be priced too high. Compare valuation.. True or false
en/544de3fe: Check yourself. In an offer for sale, who receives the money?
en/f1c0ccc1: Check yourself. A company's offer document says most of the money will repay old debt. What does Rohan learn?
en/c40a0300: Check yourself. Meena compares an IPO's price with similar listed companies. What is she checking?
en/a5742af8: Check yourself. An IPO is mostly an offer for sale by early investors. What should Rohan ask?
en/862a278d: Remember. Fresh issue: money to the company. Offer for sale: money to sellers.. Use of proceeds shows how the money will be spent.. Compare valuation with listed peers before applying.
en/7a16d4e4: Risks and cautions. IPOs: how they work and how to judge them · Beginner
en/db171ded: Before you start. Before an IPO, a stranger says: 'The grey market shows a 60% listing gain. Apply now.' Rohan applies with his savings. The shares list flat. The grey market was a rumour, and a rumour is not a promise.
en/f275d697: The grey market premium looked so confident. How wrong can it be? It is unofficial and unregulated. It can be very wrong. Treat it as noise and not as a signal. Learn the real risks instead.. Noise before the issue
en/a578eb22: Four cautions. Grey market premium, An unofficial price rumour, not reliable. Lock-in, A period when certain holders cannot sell after the IPO. SME IPO, A small company on a separate platform, usually riskier. Anchor investor, A large institution that commits just before the issue opens
en/f70ec060: It is a rumour and not a regulated price. Pre-IPO holders often cannot sell for a set time after listing. Small companies on this platform are usually riskier. Anchors show institutional interest, not a promise.. True or false
en/fc369870: Check yourself. A message says the grey market premium means the IPO will list at a big gain. What is the right view?
en/849a948a: Check yourself. Pre-IPO investors cannot sell their shares for six months after listing. What is this called?
en/49c79bbd: Check yourself. Meena sees a small company listing on the SME platform. What is a sensible view?
en/52af40f9: Check yourself. A big institution has agreed to buy shares a day before the issue opens to the public. What is it called?
en/bcd96ceb: Remember. The grey market premium is a rumour. Do not rely on it.. A lock-in stops certain holders from selling for a time.. SME IPOs are usually riskier. Anchors are not a guarantee.
en/70563474: The income statement. Reading financial statements · Beginner
en/54e05bfd: Before you start. Revenue ₹100 crore. After suppliers, staff, the bank and the tax office, ₹8 crore remains. The income statement tells that story in order: what was earned, what it cost, what was kept.
en/6691e7ab: Is revenue the same as profit? No. Revenue is money from selling goods or services in a period. EBITDA is a rough measure of operating earnings before interest, tax and write-offs. Operating margin is operating profit over revenue. Net profit is what is left after everything and belongs to the shareholders.. Earned and kept
en/94acca10: Revenue: ₹100 crore. EBITDA: a rough operating earnings measure. Operating profit, after depreciation. Net profit: what remains for shareholders.. From revenue to net profit, ₹ crore, made up. ₹8 crore kept
en/57e8362d: Check yourself. A mobile maker records the value of every phone it sold this quarter. What is this?
en/b584cfc4: Check yourself. A firm keeps ₹14 of operating profit from every ₹100 of sales. What is the operating margin?
en/23c40a33: Check yourself. After paying suppliers, staff, the bank and the tax office, ₹8 crore remains. What is this?
en/78d348ca: Remember. Revenue: money from sales in a period.. EBITDA: rough operating earnings. Operating margin = operating profit ÷ revenue.. Net profit: what remains after all costs, interest and tax.
en/4e9a1a33: The balance sheet. Reading financial statements · Beginner
en/380161a9: Before you start. If a company owns ₹100 crore and owes ₹60 crore, the owners' stake is ₹40 crore. The balance sheet is a photograph: what a company owns and owes on one day.
en/30cb939b: Why does it have two sides? One side shows assets: cash, stock, plants, customer dues. The other shows liabilities and equity. What is left after paying all liabilities belongs to the owners. Working capital is current assets minus current liabilities, the money tied up in day-to-day operations.. A photograph
en/7b06b1d2: The cash flow statement. Reading financial statements · Beginner
en/feb1ae78: Before you start. A firm reports ₹100 crore of profit but collects only ₹60 crore of cash. Profit alone cannot tell you that. The cash flow statement shows how cash actually moved.
en/08646df7: Why not just read the profit? Because profit is booked before cash moves. Operating cash flow shows what the core business generates. Capital expenditure is spending on plants and machines. Free cash flow is what is left after both. Cash conversion shows how much profit became cash.. Cash tells the truth
en/6d044d81: Cash conversion, made up. Reported profit, ₹100 crore. Operating cash collected, ₹60 crore. Cash conversion, 60%. After capex, free cash flow, e.g. ₹50 crore left
en/bae8dd31: Check yourself. A firm reports ₹100 crore of profit but collects only ₹60 crore of cash. What is the cash conversion?
en/7cfe081d: Check yourself. A cement maker builds a new kiln. What is this spending called?
en/64cbf5e6: Check yourself. After running the business and buying new machines, ₹50 crore is left. What is this?
en/84b31dc9: Check yourself. What does the cash flow statement show that profit alone cannot?
en/0a777de0: Remember. Operating cash flow: cash from the core business.. Capex: spending on long-lasting assets. Free cash flow: what remains after both.. Cash conversion = operating cash ÷ reported profit.
en/adddad8a: Story complete. The cash flow statement
en/fb51b6e0: Quality of earnings. Reading financial statements · Beginner
en/c79c3ecf: Before you start. A company books a big profit this quarter from selling land. Next quarter, the land is gone. Not all profit is equal. Some repeats, some is a one-off. Quality of earnings is how you tell them apart.
en/863ec7a3: Profit is up 40%. Good news? Ask why. An exceptional item, like a land sale, will not repeat. Accruals book a sale before cash arrives. Receivable days show how long customers take to pay. And an auditor's qualification says something is wrong with the accounts or the audit.. Repeatable or not?
en/dcd398ec: Warning signs, made up. Profit jump from land sale, an exceptional item. Sale booked in March, cash in June, an accrual. Receivable days, from 45 to 90. Audit report, could not verify a large related-party loan
en/95e4b4ce: Check yourself. A company books a large profit from selling land this quarter. What is this?
en/d736d3ae: Check yourself. A firm books a sale in March but the customer pays in June. What is this?
en/6ad198d5: Check yourself. Customers who used to pay in 45 days now take 90. What does this show?
en/14ea2f88: Check yourself. The audit report says the auditor could not verify a large loan to a related firm. What is this?
en/135ed232: Remember. Exceptional items are one-offs, not repeatable earnings.. Accruals record income when earned, not when cash moves.. Watch receivable days and auditor's qualifications.
en/8decdfda: Reading the statements together. Reading financial statements · Beginner
en/b248ead4: Before you start. A footnote reveals that the company guaranteed a loan taken by its promoter's other firm. No ratio would have shown it. The three statements connect, and the notes tell what the numbers hide. Read them as one story.
en/a2c15dd4: Which number matters most? None alone. Consolidated accounts combine the parent and its subsidiaries. Return on equity shows profit on the owners' money. Debt to equity shows reliance on borrowing. Notes to accounts explain policies, contingent liabilities and related-party deals.. One story
en/1d4d506f: Ratios, made up. Return on equity, ₹18 profit per ₹100 of owners' capital: 18%. Debt to equity, ₹150 crore against ₹100 crore: 1.5 times. Consolidated accounts, one combined profit for five subsidiaries. Notes to accounts, a footnote shows a guarantee for a promoter's firm
en/43fa62ef: Check yourself. A firm earns ₹18 for every ₹100 of owners' capital in a year. What is the return on equity?
en/5600c6fc: Check yourself. A firm has borrowed ₹150 crore against ₹100 crore of owners' money. What is the debt to equity?
en/913eb152: Check yourself. A group with five subsidiaries reports a single combined profit. What are these accounts?
en/87e68c70: Check yourself. Where would a guarantee for a promoter's other firm usually be disclosed?
en/bdad1ce2: Remember. ROE = net profit ÷ equity. Debt to equity = borrowings ÷ owners' capital.. Consolidated accounts combine parent and subsidiaries.. Notes to accounts reveal what the numbers hide.
en/9b97ce82: Story complete. Reading the statements together
en/d5b13fda: Value versus price. Valuation methods · Intermediate
en/41b35460: Before you start. A share trades at ₹650 this morning. An analyst's work says it is worth ₹800. Price is what the market asks today. Value is what the business may be worth. They are not the same, and the gap is the whole game of valuation.
en/eb2090a4: If the price is ₹650, isn't that what it is worth? It is what it trades at. Intrinsic value is an estimate, from the cash the business can generate in future. An investor wants a margin of safety, a gap between her estimate and the price paid, because estimates can be wrong.. Price and value
en/21f3004e: The share trades at ₹650. The analyst estimates ₹800. The gap is the margin of safety. Estimates can be wrong, so the gap matters.. Price against value, made up. Per share, ₹, 650, 800
en/5b781c8f: Check yourself. A share trades at ₹650 and an analyst estimates ₹800. What is the ₹800?
en/e777b0c3: Check yourself. What is a margin of safety?
en/3a270966: Check yourself. Which is preferred, ₹100 now or ₹100 after five years?
en/342a878b: Check yourself. A share changes hands at ₹650 this morning. What is ₹650?
en/c2ca5a20: Remember. Market price: where a share trades now. Intrinsic value: an estimate of worth.. Margin of safety: the gap between estimate and price paid.. A rupee today is worth more than a rupee later.
en/9ce23eb5: Discounted cash flow. Valuation methods · Intermediate
en/b8c77e7a: Before you start. A company has ₹200 crore left each year after costs, tax and new investment. What is that stream worth today? Discounted cash flow answers by adding up future cash after adjusting for time and risk.
en/ba4eb7c1: How do you value cash that has not arrived? Forecast the free cash flow to the firm. Convert each year to today's value with a discount rate, higher for riskier firms. Add a terminal value for everything beyond the forecast. WACC, the blended cost of debt and equity, is often the rate.. Adding up the future
en/6fc5cff0: A discount rate, made up. Safer business, discount at 10% a year. Riskier business, discount at 13% a year. Forecast, ten years, plus one terminal value. Result, a higher rate gives a lower value today
en/3526f023: Check yourself. Which term is the cash a business generates after expenses and investment, available to all capital providers?
en/ee4539d6: Check yourself. A riskier business is valued at 13% a year instead of 10%. What is 13%?
en/bde62ff1: Check yourself. After projecting ten years, an analyst adds one figure for everything that comes later. What is it?
en/a31d805f: Check yourself. What does WACC blend?
en/277f496e: Remember. DCF adds up future free cash flow, converted to today's value.. A higher discount rate lowers today's value.. Terminal value covers the years beyond the forecast. WACC is often the rate.
en/d80ae2eb: Before you start. A share at ₹300 earns ₹15 a year. A bank share trades at ₹210 against ₹100 of net worth. A share at 30 times earnings grows 30% a year. Four multiples, four ways to put a price next to something real.
en/1206771f: Which multiple is best? It depends on the business. P/E compares price with earnings. EV/EBITDA compares the whole business, debt included, with operating profit. P/B suits banks. PEG divides P/E by expected growth, so a P/E of 30 with 30% growth gives one.. Multiples
en/ac93ecd8: Both shares cost ₹300. A earns ₹15; B earns ₹5. A trades at 20 times, B at 60 times. Multiples compare price with earnings.. P/E from the same price, made up. P/E (times), 20, 60. EPS, ₹ (price ₹300 each), 15, 5
en/cb07ef04: Check yourself. A share priced at ₹300 earns ₹15 a year. What is the P/E?
en/1171ed28: Check yourself. A bank share trades at ₹210 against ₹100 of net worth per share. What is the P/B?
en/1f50eb13: Check yourself. A share at 30 times earnings grows earnings 30% a year. What is its PEG?
en/d6e25f98: Check yourself. Two companies carry different debt loads. Which multiple compares whole-business value against core profit?
en/461d5bd2: Remember. P/E = price ÷ EPS. P/B = price ÷ net worth per share.. EV/EBITDA compares the whole business with operating profit.. PEG = P/E ÷ expected earnings growth.
en/554c349e: Before you start. A conglomerate has telecom, retail and energy arms. One P/E cannot describe all three. Different businesses call for different tools: sum of the parts, assets, dividends or comparison with peers.
en/989b05f3: Is DCF enough for every company? No. A conglomerate is valued arm by arm. A land-rich firm is valued on its plots less its loans. A mature utility is valued on its steady dividends. A paint maker is judged against other listed paint makers.. Choose the tool
en/07883e70: Four tools. Sum of the parts, value each arm, then add. Asset-based, plots at market value less loans. Dividend discount model, present value of expected dividends. Relative valuation, compare with similar listed firms
en/34e9f69c: Check yourself. A conglomerate with telecom, retail and energy arms is valued arm by arm. What is this?
en/4eabe3ce: Check yourself. A land-rich firm is valued on its plots at market value less its loans. What is this?
en/d560e1f8: Check yourself. A mature utility pays steady payouts. Which model values it on those payouts?
en/1ad60998: Check yourself. A paint maker is judged against other listed paint makers. What is this?
en/373888f5: Remember. Sum of the parts: value each business, then add.. Asset-based: assets minus liabilities. DDM: present value of dividends.. Relative valuation: compare with similar companies.
en/8db16dc3: Testing your answer. Valuation methods · Intermediate
en/0197c41f: Before you start. An analyst's valuation says ₹900. Change one assumption and it says ₹600. A valuation is only as good as its assumptions. So test them, with sensitivity and scenarios, and beware cheap shares that are cheap for a reason.
en/3338cf1c: How sure is a target price? Not very. Sensitivity analysis shows how value moves when growth or the discount rate changes. Scenario analysis values best, base and worst stories. A target price is an estimate over a stated period. And a valuation trap looks cheap only because profits keep shrinking.. Testing the answer
en/6687a4ab: Testing assumptions, made up. Sensitivity, value at three growth rates × three discount rates. Scenarios, demand booms, holds, collapses. Target price, ₹900 in twelve months: an estimate. Valuation trap, low multiple, shrinking profits
en/217e9978: Check yourself. An analyst shows the value at three growth rates and three discount rates. What is this?
en/dc3b5570: Check yourself. A report gives separate values if demand booms, holds or collapses. What is this?
en/93e5a177: Check yourself. A report says the share could reach ₹900 in twelve months. What is ₹900?
en/62a679d5: Check yourself. A share trades at a very low multiple because its profits keep shrinking. What is this?
en/f6e11329: Remember. Sensitivity analysis changes assumptions. Scenario analysis changes stories.. A target price is an estimate, not a promise.. A valuation trap looks cheap but the business is worsening.
en/4a2b9c82: Reading a chart. Technical analysis · Beginner
en/545db99d: Before you start. Thousands of trades in a day become one small bar on a chart. A candlestick shows where the price began, how far it moved and where it ended. Charts describe what already happened. Education, not a call to trade.
en/6a6ebe3d: What is a candlestick? One bar for one period: the open, high, low and close. Many bars show a trend: up, down or sideways. The timeframe is how long each candle covers. Volume is the number of shares traded in that period.. Reading a candle
en/4666ee22: The candle opens at ₹100. It reaches a high of ₹108. It dips to a low of ₹96. It closes at ₹105.. One candle's four prices, ₹, made up. Open 100, close 105
en/bec30712: Check yourself. What does a single daily candlestick show?
en/40e294c2: Check yourself. A share has made higher peaks and higher lows for six months. What is this?
en/061449de: Check yourself. A trader checks the weekly chart for direction and the hourly chart for entry. What differs?
en/4b9679eb: Check yourself. On a breakout day, three times the usual number of shares change hands. What is this measure?
en/b2421ee3: Remember. A candlestick shows open, high, low and close for one period.. A trend can be up, down or sideways. Timeframe sets what each candle covers.. Volume is the number of shares traded.
en/7bf12d57: Support, resistance and patterns. Technical analysis · Beginner
en/5d90acc6: Before you start. A share has bounced three times near ₹480 and failed to cross ₹620 several times. Traders watch such levels because many decisions were made there before. Levels are guides, not guarantees. Education, not a call to trade.
en/837a1ca3: What are support and resistance? Support is a level where buying has tended to stop a fall. Resistance is a level where selling has tended to stop a rise. A breakout is a move through one of them, ideally on strong volume. Head and shoulders is a pattern often seen as a reversal sign.. Floors and ceilings
en/7551b52b: Levels, made up. Support, ₹480: bounced three times. Resistance, ₹620: failed several times. Breakout, a close above ₹620 on heavy volume. Head and shoulders, peak, higher peak, lower peak, then down
en/d2f10baf: Check yourself. A share has bounced three times near ₹480. What is ₹480?
en/65536d3a: Check yourself. A share has failed to cross ₹620 on several attempts. What is ₹620?
en/0b911fbe: Check yourself. A share closes above its long-standing ceiling on heavy trading. What is this?
en/fc197890: Check yourself. A rally makes a peak, a higher peak, then a lower peak before prices turn down. What is this pattern?
en/d20d58ed: Remember. Support: buying has stopped falls. Resistance: selling has stopped rises.. Breakout: a move through a level, ideally on strong volume.. Head and shoulders is often seen as a reversal sign, not a certainty.
en/72ba813d: Story complete. Support, resistance and patterns
en/8b5a6887: Before you start. The 50-day line crosses above the 200-day line. Some call it a golden cross. Indicators turn price history into simple signals, but they describe the past and can mislead. Education, not a call to trade.
en/68f3c1ae: What is a moving average? The average price over a set number of days, updated daily to smooth out noise. A 200-day line shows long-term direction. A golden cross is a short average rising above a long one. MACD uses the gap between a fast and a slow average. A trendline joins lows or highs.. Smoothing the noise
en/a56b020c: Trend tools. 200-day moving average, long-term direction. Golden cross, 50-day crosses above 200-day. MACD, 12-day and 26-day averages vs a signal line. Trendline, joins the last four higher lows
en/4267281c: Check yourself. A 200-day line shows the long-term direction of a share. What is it?
en/9ea66bfe: Check yourself. The 50-day line crosses above the 200-day line. What is this called?
en/1e14bb41: Check yourself. A line built from a 12-day and a 26-day average crosses its signal line. Which indicator is this?
en/e9e5cb35: Check yourself. A line joining the last four higher lows slopes upwards. What is this?
en/8bba0338: Remember. Moving average: average price over a set number of days.. Golden cross: a short average above a long one. MACD: gap between fast and slow averages.. A trendline joins lows or highs. Signals can fail.
en/bc6cfe7f: Momentum and volume tools. Technical analysis · Beginner
en/0705d655: Before you start. A share rallied hard for a week and its momentum reading is very high. Is it about to fall? Not necessarily. Momentum tools show how strongly price is moving, not what comes next. Education, not a call to trade.
en/58856a5c: What does RSI of 75 mean? RSI runs from 0 to 100. Above 70 hints that a rally may be stretched, called overbought. VWAP is the day's average price weighted by volume. Divergence is when price makes a new high but the indicator makes a lower high, hinting the trend may weaken.. How strong is the move?
en/859e82dc: Momentum tools. RSI above 70, rally may be stretched: overbought. Overbought, may be due for a pause or fall, not certain. VWAP, day's volume-weighted average price. Divergence, new price high, lower indicator high
en/c9cd73c2: Check yourself. A momentum indicator runs from 0 to 100. A reading above 70 hints at a stretched rally. Which is it?
en/de431c0b: Check yourself. After a sharp week-long rally, momentum readings are very high. What is the share described as?
en/11f72c7d: Check yourself. An intraday trader compares the current price with the day's volume-weighted average. What is that average?
en/10c325e9: Check yourself. A share makes a new high but its momentum reading makes a lower high. What is this?
en/0187e2dc: Remember. RSI: 0 to 100 momentum. Above 70 hints at a stretched rally.. Overbought is a hint, not a prediction. VWAP: volume-weighted average price.. Divergence: price and indicator disagree, hinting at weakness.

en/5920e190: Using it with discipline. Technical analysis · Beginner
en/9919bbbc: Before you start. A trader decides in advance to exit if the share falls five per cent. Another decides after it falls. Tools help only when the rules are set before the trade. Most trading mistakes are broken rules. Education, not a call to trade.
en/90869461: Which tool should I trust? None alone. A stop-loss is a preset exit to limit loss. A risk-reward ratio compares possible loss with possible gain. Confirmation means waiting for a second signal. Backtesting checks a rule on past data, which is not a promise for the future.. Rules first
en/108bb899: A trade plan, made up. Stop-loss, exit if the share falls 5% from entry. Risk-reward, risk ₹10 to try to make ₹30: 1 to 3. Confirmation, wait for a strong close above the ceiling. Backtest, crossover rule over ten years of prices

en/ea98c219: Check yourself. A trader waits for a strong close above the ceiling before buying. What is this?
en/0fa726e7: Check yourself. An analyst checks how a crossover rule would have done over ten years of prices. What is this?
en/a43f111d: Remember. Set the rules before the trade: stop-loss, risk-reward, confirmation.. Backtesting tests a rule on the past. It does not promise the future.. Tools help only with discipline.

en/ac31bb59: Size and growth. Industry and sector analysis · Intermediate
en/61d6fcb5: Before you start. Before judging any company, ask about its industry. How big is it? How much of it is already served? How fast can it grow? A great firm in a shrinking industry is a hard climb.
en/92149533: Why start with the industry? Because the industry sets the ceiling. Total addressable market is the full sales a product could earn if it reached every buyer. Penetration is the share of buyers already served. Market share is one company's slice. Demand drivers, like rising incomes, make customers buy more.. Size first
en/58d4f431: Competition. Industry and sector analysis · Intermediate
en/3b47169e: Before you start. A toothpaste maker raises prices slightly and sales barely change. A telecom start-up needs licences and huge spending just to begin. Profit goes to companies that rivals cannot easily copy.
en/c0588730: How do I judge competition? Porter's five forces: rivals, new entrants, substitutes, buyers and suppliers. Barriers to entry keep new firms out. An economic moat is a lasting advantage, such as a loved brand. Pricing power is raising prices without losing many customers.. Why rivals matter
